recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Do not add redundant narrative or revert the current relatesTo wording; the wording difference is due to later accepted structural changes and the current source conveys the FHIR-34159 rule in current element names.
issue_request: FHIR-34159 was a Published/Persuasive R5 Structured Documents change request for Composition in support of evidence reports. It requested adding Composition.version string 0..1, Composition.url uri 0..1, Composition.name string 0..1, Composition.useContext UsageContext 0..*, Composition.note Annotation 0..*, and narrative guidance for using Composition.relatesTo with a referenced document/composition identifier.
initial_application: The change appears to have been applied in the R5 development line through PR/merge history around HL7/fhir#1913. Commit 758e5084ff added Composition.version and relatesTo identifier guidance, commit 1c3d8dffb5 added Composition.url, Composition.name, Composition.useContext, and Composition.note, and commit 26c4cb8aad added url/version search parameters and summary/mapping follow-up.
additional_context: Composition is active in source/fhir.ini and owned by SD, so source/composition/structuredefinition-Composition.xml is current build-scope source. SD Confluence pages record the FHIR-34159 plan, approval, and application work. Later FHIR-49759 reshaped Composition.relatesTo from RelatedArtifact-style representation to a BackboneElement with type and target[x], which is why the current guidance says targetReference.identifier rather than the older resourceReference.identifier wording. The ClinicalDocument follow-up FHIR-34407 is already represented on the combined branch.
reconciliation: Published an empty audit commit because no source edit is required. The current source contains url, version, name, useContext, note, and a relatesTo comment showing how to carry only a related Bundle/Composition identifier using targetReference.identifier under the current R6 shape.
